recent_articles.title: Art in conflict zones: Nicky Chandam’s visual documentation of Manipur and the politics of performance - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Supreme Court upholds SIR exercise as an advancement towards free and fair elections - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** upheld the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls conducted by the **Election Commission of India (ECI)**, finding it constitutional and necessary for conducting free and fair elections. The court directed the ECI to refer names of electors purged in the Bihar SIR on grounds of non-citizenship to the Centre for adjudication and restore their names if found citizens. The decision ensures the integrity of the electoral rolls by addressing issues arising from population changes, migration, and inaccurate entries over time.

recent_articles.title: Probe incidents of accused being paraded in underwear: APDR writes to West Bengal Human Rights Commission - The Hindu

The organization argues that these actions violate human rights and are a form of "criminal force" by law enforcement.

recent_articles.title: Rate at which West Bengal tribunals restoring names of deleted electors proves genuine voters not allowed to vote: Prasenjit Bose - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prasenjit Bose**, chairperson of the SIR Committee of West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee, stated that appellate tribunals have restored the names of 4,043 electors (61%) from over 25 lakh appeals against deletions in West Bengal.  He emphasized that this evidence demonstrates how genuine voters were wrongfully deleted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. **Bose** also pointed out that while the Supreme Court upheld the SIR exercise in Bihar, a clear judicial forum for electors to challenge decisions is necessary. The SIR resulted in 27 lakh voters being excluded from West Bengal electoral rolls on April 7th, weeks before the Assembly polls, with significant deletions occurring in two Muslim-dominated districts.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool MLA arrested, several leaders quit party post - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: CPI(M), CPI: India's communists once ruled millions. What happened to them?

While the party has seen its influence diminish across various regions, it remains politically relevant in Kerala and continues to hold onto some support in other states like Tamil Nadu. The decline is attributed to factors including economic stagnation, changing political landscapes, and a shift towards identity politics. Despite these challenges, the CPI (M) insists on adapting to the modern economy and seeks to revitalize its presence within the Indian political landscape.
